notes.note: This beardtongue is grown in small groups in borders, pollinator gardens or naturalized areas. Give it at least 6 hours of direct sun a day, or 2 to 6 hours in part shade. It prefers well-drained loam that is moist to dry, and tolerates clay that drains well. It is suited to acidic soil.

notes.note: Orange coneflower is grown in perennial beds, borders and naturalized areas. Give it full sun if you can, though it tolerates partial shade. Plant it in humus-rich soil that holds moisture but drains well. That said, it does fine in any soil that is not soggy. Once it is established, it can handle drought.

notes.note: Horned violet is a tufted perennial that spreads by creeping stems. Grow it as a perennial in borders and woodland gardens, or as an annual in window boxes and containers. You can also use it as a ground cover. Plant it where it gets full sun or part shade. Give it fertile, humus-rich soil that is moist but drains well.
